title: ARSIA Audit Query Response
description: Cursor-paginated response from the audit trail query endpoint (GET /.well-known/arsia/audit). Contains ArsiaAuditRecord objects ordered by processed_at ascending with pagination metadata; for a query with chain_id, contains that chain's entries (records and tombstones) ordered by chain_seq ascending. Defined in ARSIA-State.md §7.4. Requires arsiaprotocol.audit.read capability. The endpoint supports 12 query parameters: from_agent, to_agent, after (RFC 3339), before (RFC 3339), event_type, compliance_profile, human_oversight_status, payment_reference, limit (integer, default 100, max 1000), after_record_id (cursor-based pagination), chain_id (chain retrieval, ARSIA-State.md §7.2), after_chain_seq (integer cursor for chain queries).

records.description: Array of ArsiaAuditRecord objects ordered by processed_at ascending; for a query with chain_id, the chain's entries — records and tombstones — ordered by chain_seq ascending. Per ARSIA-State.md §7.4. The schema enforces the structural coherence of a response that contains a tombstone (every entry carries chain_id and chain_seq; next_cursor, when present, is an integer chain_seq). Whether the response matches the query parameters — tombstones only for a query with chain_id, entries of the queried chain only — is a runtime obligation the response alone cannot show. Chained records are not limited to chain queries.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query filters regardless of limit. Per ARSIA-State.md §7.4.

has_more.description: Whether additional records exist beyond the current page. Per ARSIA-State.md §7.4.

next_cursor.description: The record_id (UUID v4) of the last record in the current page, passed as after_record_id; for a query with chain_id, the chain_seq (integer) of the last returned entry, passed as after_chain_seq. Present when has_more is true. Per ARSIA-State.md §7.4.

allOf.$comment: State §7.4: a response that contains a tombstone is a chain response (structural coherence only)
